To find g(x), we need to integrate g'(x) with respect to x.  \\ \int g'(x) dx = \int (6x - 12) dx\\ g(x) = 6 \int x dx - 12 \int dx\\ g(x) = 6 \cdot \frac{x^2}{2} - 12x + C\\ g(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + C\\ We are given that the graph of g passes through the point (1, 2). This means that g(1) = 2. We can use this information to find the value of the constant C. \\ g(1) = 3(1)^2 - 12(1) + C = 2\\ 3 - 12 + C = 2\\ -9 + C = 2\\ C = 2 + 9\\ C = 11\\ Therefore, g(x) = 3x^2 - 12x + 11.
